order: Grade the initial forty-item corpus blind against the sealed reference pass. Record the result against the pre-registered threshold of at least thirty-six of forty items. If the threshold is missed, redraw the class borders and apply the redraw to the plan, but do not simply patch individual items in isolation. Diagnose the root cause of any concentrated disagreement pattern before changing anything. Add a precedence rule to the preamble: recall signals are hints alone, and the requested work product plus the border rule decide from intake text, not a signal word standing in for it; rename the relevant column to match. Amend the border rules implicated by the disagreements, confine any new rule to where a genuine gap is found, and add phase-ordering rules for diagnosis-before-implementation and composite orders. Record the reference pass, the disagreement ledger, the redraw, and a post-redraw resolution of every flagged item while noting it is a grading reference and never a validation.
claims: The blind pass graded thirty-one of forty items at 77.5 percent against the pre-registered threshold of at least thirty-six of forty, with two ambiguities at the cap. Nine disagreements spanned nine distinct pairs, ten counting the ambiguity, and none repeated, so no three-pair combination was triggered. The redraw was applied, adding a precedence rule, amending the implicated border rules, adding new ones only where a genuine gap was found, and introducing two phase rules.
